title: Public delegations on the 2026 budget
subtitle: Day shelter funding, winter bike lane maintenance, Route 98 transit delay, park stewards, arts, physician recruitment and food bank bus access.
overview: Council held a special meeting devoted to public delegations on the proposed 2026 budget. Residents and organizations spoke for up to five minutes each. No budget amendments were voted on; those are expected at the budget meeting on November 26.

Delegates asked council to fund a daytime drop-in space shared by two local service organizations, to keep winter maintenance on on-road bike lanes, and to restore the Route 98 transit enhancement that was deferred to 2027. Others asked for free bus tickets for food bank clients and spoke about deferrals, rising taxes and the Emma Earl Bridge. The mayor said arts and culture funding and the park stewardship program were already back in the budget. Delegates also backed physician recruitment funding, the Community Benefits Agreement with the Guelph Tool Library and the Guelph Gateway trail project.

After staff answered questions, councillors stated intentions to bring forward amendments. The mayor said the proposed city and outside board increases could add up to a combined tax increase of about 8.5 to 8.6 per cent, and that outside boards will be rescheduled to February. The only motions were by-law approval and adjournment {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved a group of by-laws, including 21144, 21145 and 21168 through 21174, subject to Section 284.11 (4) of the Municipal Act {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Delegates supporting the daytime drop-in space said it fills a service gap, eases pressure on the downtown Quebec Street site by splitting hours between two locations, and reduces strain on hospitals and crisis services. A councillor asked for details on locations and hours.

Several delegates opposed ending winter maintenance of on-road bike lanes. They said it would hurt safety, accessibility and affordability for people without cars, and conflicts with Vision Zero and mode share goals. Staff said the lanes would not be cleared and the public would be told they are closed.

Transit delegates said deferring Route 98 would delay the wider grid network and leave students and hospital imaging clinic patients without evening and weekend service. The mayor and staff noted the enhancement had been planned to start in September, so the deferral to 2027 is partial.

A food bank delegate asked for bus tickets to help clients without transport reach the Crimea Street site. Councillors asked why the free affordable bus pass tiers do not already cover this, and staff pointed to application paperwork and a possible on-demand stop until Route 97 serves the area.
Other delegates urged restraint, citing rising property taxes and operating and capital budgets. Another said deferrals tend to repeat, and called for funding services properly.
